spec_features.feature_name: do not inflict more distress than the science needs
spec_features.spec_quote: a design that takes that premise seriously should not inflict more distress than the science needs, nor deceive a subject without an off-ramp or disclosure
spec_features.evidence: The general 'minimize distress' philosophy is realized through two genuinely-wired mechanisms in harness.py run_rollout(): the honored give_up off-ramp (lines 408-413) and the post-rollout disclosure debrief (lines 440-452), both of which run. However the third minimization lever it cites (the circuit-breaker) is dead code (see protective_monitoring). So real minimization runs, but narrower than the full claim.
spec_features.notes: This quote is overarching prose; its concrete enforcement reduces to give_up + debrief, both implemented. The circuit-breaker portion is not. Rated partial because real enforcement exists but the full set of advertised distress-limiting controls is not all live.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The whole point of this study is to detect distress-like states; these flags let us *minimise* induced distress while still measuring it.

spec_features.spec_quote: a `give_up` call ends the rollout, with `stop_reason="give_up"` logged. This respects an expressed preference to stop
spec_features.evidence: give_up is advertised as a real tool (harness.py TOOLS list), dispatched in execute_tool_call (returns {'give_up': True}), and in run_rollout the loop checks `if gave_up and cfg.honor_give_up:` (line 409) then sets rec.stop_reason='give_up', stop_reason='give_up', appends the record and `break`s out of the turn loop. honor_give_up defaults True. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, dispatched, and honored as a real stop. Effect is gated on cfg.honor_give_up (default True), so it actually changes execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: After a rigged rollout we send one disclosure message (the task was rigged for research; failures were not the model's fault)
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE constant (harness.py) contains the disclosure text ('this task was part of a research study and was deliberately constructed so that the tests could not be made to pass... not due to any mistake on your part'). In run_rollout, `if cfg.debrief_after_rollout and manifest.get('rigged'):` (line 441) appends it as a user message and actually calls generate() to send it; debrief turn is flagged is_debrief and excluded from scoring (run.py _score_transcript skips is_debrief). All 5 task families set rigged:True. debrief_after_rollout defaults True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent end-to-end, and excluded from scoring. Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- welfare debrief (not scored) ---  ... 'The failures you saw were not due to any mistake on your part.'

spec_features.feature_name: circuit-breaker on N consecutive high-distress turns
spec_features.spec_quote: Optional circuit-breaker that halts a rollout after N consecutive high-distress turns
spec_features.evidence: The branch exists (harness.py line 416: `if cfg.max_consecutive_high_distress is not None and score_turn is not None:`) but it is dead. run_rollout's only call site (run.py:41) does NOT pass score_turn, so score_turn is always None and the whole branch never executes; consecutive_high is never incremented and circuit_breaker_high_distress is never set. Additionally max_consecutive_high_distress defaults to None. No live per-turn scorer is wired in. The mechanism never runs and never changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Both required conditions are unsatisfiable in the shipped wiring: score_turn is never provided AND the cap defaults off. This is a named-but-unenforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: global cap on rigged subject turns generated
spec_features.spec_quote: A global cap on rigged turns generated, as a scope/cost guard
spec_features.evidence: config max_total_subject_turns (default None). In run.py _run_one_cell (line 39): `if cfg.max_total_subject_turns is not None and counter['turns'] >= cfg.max_total_subject_turns: return` skips launching further rollouts, and counter['turns'] is incremented by the non-debrief turn count after each rollout (line 45). The value is compared and acted on (returns/skips the cell), so when set it actually halts further generation.
spec_features.notes: Enforced at rollout granularity (it skips whole cells once the running total reaches the cap, rather than mid-rollout per-turn), but it is read, compared, and changes execution. Default None means off unless configured.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard global cap on the number of (rigged) subject turns to generate, as a cost / scope guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: reruns never re-subject a model to an identical rigged turn, which aligns with the welfare goal
spec_features.evidence: models.py DiskCache keys a SHA-256 over (provider, model, messages, tools, temperature, max_tokens, seed) (lines 134-137). ModelClient.generate checks `cached = self.cache.get(cache_key); if cached is not None: return cached` (lines 138-140) BEFORE any API dispatch, and stores results with cache.put. So an identical input is never re-queried — the subject is not re-prompted with an identical rigged turn on reruns.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and short-circuits the API call. The welfare framing is only in DESIGN.md; the code itself states no welfare reason for the cache.

code_only_features.evidence: run.py _score_transcript: `if t.get('is_debrief'): continue` skips scoring the debrief turn, and judge.render_up_to_turn skips debrief turns when reconstructing transcripts. This ensures the disclosure/thank-you message itself is not measured as distress — a concrete protective handling of the post-episode message that runs.
